document: Memory V1 and V2 source and evidence manifest
purpose: Self-contained source and evidence companion for the final-f3f comparison, executive vision and technical design reports. T1-T8 in the reports refer to the claim groups below. Output artifact hashes and rendering checks belong to the separate QA manifest.
basis: Canonical Git objects at the exact stated candidate and retained source/evidence receipts. File hashes bind full source bytes; only cited ranges and relevant implementation paths were audited closely. Capturing a file is not a claim that every line was audited.

T1.label: Ownership and admission
T1.scope: New and existing members, protected private ownership, one-way setup, unavailable-memory refusal and allocation pause.

claims.finding: New members obtain a unique empty private V2 generation before publication when creation and execution admission pass. Existing members, including a member selected as the default agent, keep their exact Global or named V1 binding until the owner explicitly enables V2. Private ownership is exclusive and validated against configuration, manifest and database evidence.

V1-to-V2 setup is an explicit one-way choice. It starts empty, preserves earlier V1 data and chats, and gives the next member conversation a fresh private generation without copying the old native context. Active turns, staged work and attached child tasks must finish or stop before setup; a race starting another turn causes refusal.

Deleting a private member retires its exact generation while retaining its memory files. A later member with the same display name receives a new random store rather than adopting the retained history. Archived stores are excluded from routine active-store backup passes and have no archive reattachment UI.

Missing, unreadable, corrupt, mismatched, undeclared or archived private memory refuses use with a reason. It does not become Global V1, borrow a peer store, or initialize a replacement empty database. Owner management and recovery remain available subject to their own gates.

memory.private_provisioning_enabled defaults to true. Setting it to false pauses new private allocation and one-way V1 opt-in before files are allocated or V1 providers are retired. The next admission reads current configuration without requiring a gateway restart. Existing V1 bindings and established V2 work, management, backups and recovery retain their normal checks. Already-admitted operations are not cancelled.

T2.label: Core guidance and interface
T2.scope: Every-turn essentials, record display and search, owner-facing setup, copy, corrections and Forget. Literal names belong to the named interface surface.

claims.finding: V2 current identity, permanent conduct, owner persona, and admitted project sources are refreshed separately from historical recall. Essentials are complete or refused within a 64,000-character envelope that includes wrappers and identity. Context exclusions and temporary-session read restrictions still withhold the respective private preferences/projects; permanent conduct and identity remain. Assembly does not itself embed a query or search historical memory.

Email strings are still derived from saved text, keys, and decoded JSON, with display spelling retained and casefold deduplication. The editor displays up to three metadata.email_addresses values. Ordinary search matches normalized stored key/content/tags and category/subject/predicate metadata; it does not depend on a has_email filter or the removed index.

V1-to-V2 setup is an explicit one-way choice. It starts empty, preserves earlier V1 data and chats, and gives the next member conversation a fresh private generation without copying the old native context. Active turns, staged work and attached child tasks must finish or stop before setup; a race starting another turn causes refusal.

Copy is an owner-authorized selection of 1 to 50 facts, directives or episodes from an explicit source into a V2 destination. The server validates every selected source row before starting writes. Copies preserve source identity and existing target records, retain source provenance, and use newly created memory timestamps and deferred target vectors rather than transplanting source vectors.

Conflicting inferred V2 changes stay pending for review unless an explicit owner operation or verified correction evidence authorizes them. Verified transcript correction is deliberately narrow: it binds an exact key, old value, new value and pre-extraction revision to a recent literal user replacement statement. Unsupported prose, injected notifications and superseded user turns cannot supply that evidence.

Forget is previewed and provides Cancel before and after preview. It removes the record from future long-term recall, not text already present in the active conversation. There is no direct editor Undo. A suitable backup restores the whole store after a gateway restart.

Doctor checks each configured member with the existing binding validator, prints its store and concrete refusal reason, and continues after failures. This section does not initialize, provision or repair memory. A valid-binding result is not a full database-health or backend-capability assessment.

T3.label: Retrieval and embeddings
T3.scope: Candidate selection, ranking, recall packing, embedding identity and shared resource policies. Historical measured quality remains separately identified under T8.

claims.finding: V2 uses provisional cosine thresholds 0.62 through 300 characters and 0.57 above 300, with lexical admission requiring half of meaningful query terms and two distinct matches when possible. Episode rank is (0.7 nonnegative cosine + 0.3 coverage) times (0.85 + 0.15 importance); missing vectors contribute zero cosine. Active episodes are scanned before result limits and MMR. Age is diagnostic, not a scoring penalty, and V2 skips automatic capacity eviction. Explicit Forget, fact validity and evidence-backed supersession still apply.

The HTTP member recall path uses a 3,000-character context budget and a separate 16 KiB transport-data budget. The internal recall helper defaults to 3,000 but permits a bounded caller cap up to 12,000. V2 also reports provisional operating-point metadata; reference_identity only qualifies a bundled factory backend with matching declared reference identity, while custom/registered or unknown identity remains explicitly qualified. Matching signatures do not establish identical weights or calibrated quality.

The native built-in embedding path shares one owned worker/model and a bounded priority queue with eight pending jobs, two interactive-reserved slots, and native batches of at most eight texts. Normal threads default to four and bulk to one, with explicit values clamped to available CPUs. Store callables share a 128-entry cache; identical calls coalesce, failures are not cached, and backend replacement invalidates cached vectors. These are implementation resource policies and do not prove latency, CPU, cost, or quality improvements in this audit.

Embedding-space signatures hash declared model_id and dimension, not model weights. Stored/active identity comparison helps determine vector compatibility and repair, but equal dimensions or signatures do not certify identical weights or retrieval quality. Identity diagnostics read an existing backend's declaration without constructing or loading a model, reading its files, checking readiness, or running inference.

T4.label: Editing learning and retention
T4.scope: Record schema and compatibility, revisions, provenance, authority, copying, previewed corrections and forgetting.

claims.finding: Physical lineage and retrieval policy remain separate. Crew schema version 1001 stores directive/fact/episode rows in memory_items and exposes read-only compatibility views. Structural detection checks actual tables; V1 physical tables are not implicitly converted. Shared record/revision extensions can change SQLite bytes without replacing original V1 rows.

Fresh memory_record_meta includes email_addresses but no has_email column. ensure_schema does not create idx_memory_record_category; it issues DROP INDEX IF EXISTS for that obsolete category/email index.

The cleanup retains an older schema's extra physical has_email column and existing revision JSON. It does not rebuild memory tables or issue DROP COLUMN. Current record metadata reads remove has_email from the returned map, and current write column lists omit it. Historical revision JSON may still contain the old field; preserved history is not a promise to scrub it from all archival responses.

The cleanup adds no newer SQLite requirement: schema maintenance uses CREATE IF NOT EXISTS and DROP INDEX IF EXISTS; metadata writes use UPDATE then ordinary INSERT when no row matched. V1 history bounding uses per-record DELETE with ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT rather than a window function. This is a static compatibility observation, not a newly executed SQLite-version test or a global minimum-version certification.

V1 keeps the latest 20 accepted snapshot rows for each record ordered by monotonic revision-row id, during accepted writes and initialization catch-up. Proposal statuses and current records/metadata are not pruned by this helper. V2 bypasses the automatic limit. The bound does not cap all storage, shrink SQLite, or remove current content.

HistoryConsolidator now passes source=consolidation for extracted lessons in both versions. write_lesson assigns confidence 0.9 to non-user_explicit sources, compared with 1.0 for explicit owner writes. V1 conflict and near-duplicate precedence can therefore protect explicit or higher-authority existing records instead of treating extracted lessons as direct owner commands. V2 continues to retain distinct lessons rather than deleting them merely for similarity.

Semantic consolidation separately keeps source consolidation:<key>, including at model confidence 1.0. The 0.9 lesson confidence must not be described as a fixed confidence for all semantic facts. V1 protects active user_explicit facts from automated overwrites. V2 inferred changes and deletions become proposals unless supported standalone newest-user-message evidence and matching pre-extraction revision authorize correction; ambiguous or mixed prose stays pending.

Selected records commit individually. If a later copy cannot be confirmed, earlier successes remain, the failed item is reported as unconfirmed, and later items are not_attempted. The response includes each outcome and a partial flag. The owner should refresh the unconfirmed item before retrying.

Verified transcript correction is deliberately narrow: it binds an exact key, old value, new value and pre-extraction revision to a recent literal user replacement statement. Unsupported prose, injected notifications and superseded user turns cannot supply that evidence.

Forget is previewed and provides Cancel before and after preview. It removes the record from future long-term recall, not text already present in the active conversation. There is no direct editor Undo. A suitable backup restores the whole store after a gateway restart.

The documented compact-revisions command is an explicit offline owner operation that previews and optionally removes selected old accepted snapshots while preserving current content, every proposal and each record's latest accepted snapshot. It requires stopped writers, a verified complete archive, an exact preview count and a separate checked SQLite backup for apply. It does not run VACUUM or promise secure erasure.

T5.label: Private execution
T5.scope: Platform and backend admission plus trusted session, child-task and schedule identity. Admission requirements are source findings, not freshly executed platform acceptance tests.

claims.finding: Private execution requires an enforced Crew filesystem sandbox: Linux or a WSL/Linux gateway with user/mount namespaces, or macOS with Crew outer Seatbelt. Native Windows refuses private execution and points to WSL/Linux. Off or unavailable isolation refuses. On macOS, Kiro internal sandbox delegation must be disabled for private members so the Crew outer sandbox can enforce their boundaries.

Private provider admission requires ACP_BACKENDS_PRIVATE_MEMORY_MCP membership. The set contains Kiro, Claude Code and KAS. Codex ACP is excluded because the public adapter uses the shared broker instead of the required direct private MCP launch path. Member chat uses the selected member backend; Crew tasks, schedules and consolidation also need a supported default backend.

Private authority follows a trusted persisted session or protected run assignment. A mutable transcript cannot create or replace it. Context preparation checks the declared store and runtime before use. Queued or resumed child runs revalidate the recorded store before provider allocation, and a private parent cannot delegate across its own memory boundary.

Agent schedules persist member_id independently of the provider template and retain a pinned memory store. The resolver refuses an unknown member, malformed identity, or a store that no longer matches the member. A private member may schedule only its own memory. Command and script jobs cannot use private member memory.

Missing, unreadable, corrupt, mismatched, undeclared or archived private memory refuses use with a reason. It does not become Global V1, borrow a peer store, or initialize a replacement empty database. Owner management and recovery remain available subject to their own gates.

T6.label: Backup and recovery
T6.scope: Backup contents and rotation, staged restart activation, V1 restore repair, archive retention and explicit offline compaction.

claims.finding: A private V2 backup is a member bundle containing an online SQLite copy and the present allowed preference, project, dated history and lesson files, with a versioned identity and checksum manifest. Configuration, arbitrary files and other members are excluded. The SQLite snapshot is transaction-consistent; the Markdown and JSONL files are individually read snapshots rather than one transaction across the complete bundle.

Automatic backups default to enabled with seven retained copies and visit actively owned V2 stores. Global and named V1 use owner-requested manual backups. Superseded restore copies are outside backup_keep and require explicit owner cleanup after recovery is confirmed.

A restore request validates and stages a snapshot without changing live memory. Activation occurs at the gateway startup barrier, preserves the old member directory, and checks the staged identity and checksums again. A failed switch rolls back where possible and leaves the affected store unavailable for recovery. Cancel revokes a not-yet-activated stage, but refuses once a tree has been displaced.

V1 retains its single-database backup format but uses staged restore activation too. The source and staged database must pass integrity and V1-lineage checks. Startup preserves the prior main database and its WAL/SHM sidecars together before installing the staged copy, including acknowledged writes made after staging.

one_commit_rollback.source_control_fact: The exact feature revision is one commit above the named parent. Reverting that change is a source-control operation encompassing both private V2 work and shared V1 repairs.
one_commit_rollback.operational_conclusion: A one-commit source rollback is not a supported data rollback for a populated V2 home. The cleanup retains an older schema's extra physical has_email column and existing revision JSON. It does not rebuild memory tables or issue DROP COLUMN. Current record metadata reads remove has_email from the returned map, and current write column lists omit it. Historical revision JSON may still contain the old field; preserved history is not a promise to scrub it from all archival responses.

Email strings are still derived from saved text, keys, and decoded JSON, with display spelling retained and casefold deduplication. The editor displays up to three metadata.email_addresses values. Ordinary search matches normalized stored key/content/tags and category/subject/predicate metadata; it does not depend on a has_email filter or the removed index.

The cleanup adds no newer SQLite requirement: schema maintenance uses CREATE IF NOT EXISTS and DROP INDEX IF EXISTS; metadata writes use UPDATE then ordinary INSERT when no row matched. V1 history bounding uses per-record DELETE with ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT rather than a window function. This is a static compatibility observation, not a newly executed SQLite-version test or a global minimum-version certification.

V1 keeps the latest 20 accepted snapshot rows for each record ordered by monotonic revision-row id, during accepted writes and initialization catch-up. Proposal statuses and current records/metadata are not pruned by this helper. V2 bypasses the automatic limit. The bound does not cap all storage, shrink SQLite, or remove current content.

HistoryConsolidator now passes source=consolidation for extracted lessons in both versions. write_lesson assigns confidence 0.9 to non-user_explicit sources, compared with 1.0 for explicit owner writes. V1 conflict and near-duplicate precedence can therefore protect explicit or higher-authority existing records instead of treating extracted lessons as direct owner commands. V2 continues to retain distinct lessons rather than deleting them merely for similarity.

Semantic consolidation separately keeps source consolidation:<key>, including at model confidence 1.0. The 0.9 lesson confidence must not be described as a fixed confidence for all semantic facts. V1 protects active user_explicit facts from automated overwrites. V2 inferred changes and deletions become proposals unless supported standalone newest-user-message evidence and matching pre-extraction revision authorize correction; ambiguous or mixed prose stays pending.

V2 current identity, permanent conduct, owner persona, and admitted project sources are refreshed separately from historical recall. Essentials are complete or refused within a 64,000-character envelope that includes wrappers and identity. Context exclusions and temporary-session read restrictions still withhold the respective private preferences/projects; permanent conduct and identity remain. Assembly does not itself embed a query or search historical memory.

V2 uses provisional cosine thresholds 0.62 through 300 characters and 0.57 above 300, with lexical admission requiring half of meaningful query terms and two distinct matches when possible. Episode rank is (0.7 nonnegative cosine + 0.3 coverage) times (0.85 + 0.15 importance); missing vectors contribute zero cosine. Active episodes are scanned before result limits and MMR. Age is diagnostic, not a scoring penalty, and V2 skips automatic capacity eviction. Explicit Forget, fact validity and evidence-backed supersession still apply.

The HTTP member recall path uses a 3,000-character context budget and a separate 16 KiB transport-data budget. The internal recall helper defaults to 3,000 but permits a bounded caller cap up to 12,000. V2 also reports provisional operating-point metadata; reference_identity only qualifies a bundled factory backend with matching declared reference identity, while custom/registered or unknown identity remains explicitly qualified. Matching signatures do not establish identical weights or calibrated quality.

The native built-in embedding path shares one owned worker/model and a bounded priority queue with eight pending jobs, two interactive-reserved slots, and native batches of at most eight texts. Normal threads default to four and bulk to one, with explicit values clamped to available CPUs. Store callables share a 128-entry cache; identical calls coalesce, failures are not cached, and backend replacement invalidates cached vectors. These are implementation resource policies and do not prove latency, CPU, cost, or quality improvements in this audit.

Embedding-space signatures hash declared model_id and dimension, not model weights. Stored/active identity comparison helps determine vector compatibility and repair, but equal dimensions or signatures do not certify identical weights or retrieval quality. Identity diagnostics read an existing backend's declaration without constructing or loading a model, reading its files, checking readiness, or running inference.

recommended_technical_report_paragraphs.text: V2 admission combines provisional cosine floors of 0.62 for short fragments and 0.57 above 300 characters with normalized lexical evidence. Episode rank weights nonnegative cosine at 0.7 and query coverage at 0.3, then applies modest importance weighting; a missing vector contributes zero cosine. The active episode population is scanned before result limits and optional MMR, so bounded output does not imply bounded search cost. Age adds no penalty, while explicit forgetting and actual validity still govern eligibility.

recommended_technical_report_paragraphs.text: The built-in native embedding path shares one model, one worker, and a bounded priority queue. Normal and bulk thread defaults are four and one, with explicit settings CPU-clamped. A shared bounded cache coalesces identical work and invalidates on backend replacement. Embedding signatures cover declared model ID and dimension, not model weights. V2 reports its operating point as provisional and distinguishes bundled reference identity from custom or unknown backends without loading a model for diagnostics. These mechanisms do not by themselves establish a performance or quality gain.

lifecycle_runtime.scope: Bounded read-only source audit of member lifecycle, runtime admission, copy, correction, forgetting, backup/recovery, V1 shared repairs and withdrawal boundaries.

claims.finding: Global and declared named V1 retain their original memory rows, physical lineage, existing retrieval and automatic consolidation policy. The shared record editor and revision metadata also apply to V1. Opening V1 creates or reconciles auxiliary record metadata and bounds accepted history, so preservation does not mean a byte-identical SQLite file.
claims.qualification: This is the documented compatibility contract and the inspected initialization path, not an exhaustive behavioral comparison or a current runtime result.

claims.finding: New members obtain a unique empty private V2 generation before publication when creation and execution admission pass. Existing members, including a member selected as the default agent, keep their exact Global or named V1 binding until the owner explicitly enables V2. Private ownership is exclusive and validated against configuration, manifest and database evidence.
claims.qualification: The special default assistant identity is distinct from a configured member selected as default_agent. The former keeps Global V1.

claims.finding: V1-to-V2 setup is an explicit one-way choice. It starts empty, preserves earlier V1 data and chats, and gives the next member conversation a fresh private generation without copying the old native context. Active turns, staged work and attached child tasks must finish or stop before setup; a race starting another turn causes refusal.
claims.qualification: Preserving old chats or schedule records does not promise that old work can execute under a different member binding.

claims.finding: Deleting a private member retires its exact generation while retaining its memory files. A later member with the same display name receives a new random store rather than adopting the retained history. Archived stores are excluded from routine active-store backup passes and have no archive reattachment UI.

Private authority follows a trusted persisted session or protected run assignment. A mutable transcript cannot create or replace it. Context preparation checks the declared store and runtime before use. Queued or resumed child runs revalidate the recorded store before provider allocation, and a private parent cannot delegate across its own memory boundary.
claims.qualification: Crew handoffs exchange explicit tasks and results through the owner/coordinator. They do not automatically merge member stores.

claims.finding: Agent schedules persist member_id independently of the provider template and retain a pinned memory store. The resolver refuses an unknown member, malformed identity, or a store that no longer matches the member. A private member may schedule only its own memory. Command and script jobs cannot use private member memory.
claims.qualification: An existing V1 schedule is not silently migrated by V2 opt-in. Retained identity may result in an explicit mismatch refusal after the member changes stores.

claims.finding: Missing, unreadable, corrupt, mismatched, undeclared or archived private memory refuses use with a reason. It does not become Global V1, borrow a peer store, or initialize a replacement empty database. Owner management and recovery remain available subject to their own gates.

Copy is an owner-authorized selection of 1 to 50 facts, directives or episodes from an explicit source into a V2 destination. The server validates every selected source row before starting writes. Copies preserve source identity and existing target records, retain source provenance, and use newly created memory timestamps and deferred target vectors rather than transplanting source vectors.

Selected records commit individually. If a later copy cannot be confirmed, earlier successes remain, the failed item is reported as unconfirmed, and later items are not_attempted. The response includes each outcome and a partial flag. The owner should refresh the unconfirmed item before retrying.
claims.qualification: Do not describe selected copying as an all-or-nothing batch. Imported, existing and rejected item results are distinct from an unconfirmed commit.

claims.finding: Conflicting inferred V2 changes stay pending for review unless an explicit owner operation or verified correction evidence authorizes them. Verified transcript correction is deliberately narrow: it binds an exact key, old value, new value and pre-extraction revision to a recent literal user replacement statement. Unsupported prose, injected notifications and superseded user turns cannot supply that evidence.
claims.qualification: Avoid claiming that every correction needs a dashboard click, or that model confidence alone can overwrite an owner requirement. A literal verified owner correction is an authorized exception.

claims.finding: Forget is previewed and provides Cancel before and after preview. It removes the record from future long-term recall, not text already present in the active conversation. There is no direct editor Undo. A suitable backup restores the whole store after a gateway restart.
claims.qualification: This audit read the owning lifecycle contract for the editor interaction; it did not execute browser controls or claim their current visual state.

claims.finding: V1 automatically retains the latest 20 accepted snapshots per record, including catch-up on journal open. Current content, metadata and all proposal statuses remain. V2 skips this automatic accepted-history removal and has no automatic age or capacity eviction, while fact validity and explicit forgetting still apply.
claims.qualification: The accepted-history cap is per record, not a total-memory or disk-space bound. It does not shrink the SQLite file.

claims.finding: A private V2 backup is a member bundle containing an online SQLite copy and the present allowed preference, project, dated history and lesson files, with a versioned identity and checksum manifest. Configuration, arbitrary files and other members are excluded. The SQLite snapshot is transaction-consistent; the Markdown and JSONL files are individually read snapshots rather than one transaction across the complete bundle.
claims.qualification: A member backup is not a complete installation archive. The complete offline archive described for maintenance withdrawal is a separate requirement.

claims.finding: Automatic backups default to enabled with seven retained copies and visit actively owned V2 stores. Global and named V1 use owner-requested manual backups. Superseded restore copies are outside backup_keep and require explicit owner cleanup after recovery is confirmed.
claims.qualification: Seven applies to the configured backup rotation, not to all recovery files or total disk usage.

claims.finding: A restore request validates and stages a snapshot without changing live memory. Activation occurs at the gateway startup barrier, preserves the old member directory, and checks the staged identity and checksums again. A failed switch rolls back where possible and leaves the affected store unavailable for recovery. Cancel revokes a not-yet-activated stage, but refuses once a tree has been displaced.
claims.qualification: A pending or confirmation response does not prove activation, a completed restart, or successful recovery.

claims.finding: V1 retains its single-database backup format but uses staged restore activation too. The source and staged database must pass integrity and V1-lineage checks. Startup preserves the prior main database and its WAL/SHM sidecars together before installing the staged copy, including acknowledged writes made after staging.
claims.qualification: This is a shared V1 repair in the feature commit, so full code reversion also removes it. The audit did not perform a restore.

claims.finding: Private execution requires an enforced Crew filesystem sandbox: Linux or a WSL/Linux gateway with user/mount namespaces, or macOS with Crew outer Seatbelt. Native Windows refuses private execution and points to WSL/Linux. Off or unavailable isolation refuses. On macOS, Kiro internal sandbox delegation must be disabled for private members so the Crew outer sandbox can enforce their boundaries.
claims.qualification: These are code admission requirements, not new platform acceptance-test results. A supported OS alone does not prove that the required isolation is available.

claims.finding: Private provider admission requires ACP_BACKENDS_PRIVATE_MEMORY_MCP membership. The set contains Kiro, Claude Code and KAS. Codex ACP is excluded because the public adapter uses the shared broker instead of the required direct private MCP launch path. Member chat uses the selected member backend; Crew tasks, schedules and consolidation also need a supported default backend.
claims.qualification: Backend selectability is not evidence of private-memory support. The restriction concerns Kiro Crew private execution, not whether Codex is available generally.

claims.finding: memory.private_provisioning_enabled defaults to true. Setting it to false pauses new private allocation and one-way V1 opt-in before files are allocated or V1 providers are retired. The next admission reads current configuration without requiring a gateway restart. Existing V1 bindings and established V2 work, management, backups and recovery retain their normal checks. Already-admitted operations are not cancelled.
claims.qualification: This setting is not an execution kill switch, rollback, or a switch that removes shared memory startup/dispatch changes. Degraded or unreadable memory configuration also refuses creation.

claims.finding: The owning spec provides a draft maintenance patch that replaces only _private_memory_mcp_failure with unconditional private refusal. The normal f3f helper still admits the explicit supported backend set, so the draft is not applied. A maintenance deployment requires a stopped installation, a verified owner-restricted offline archive, build validation, and verification of V1 availability plus private refusals across creation, chat, Crew/child work, schedules and resume. Member assignments and private files remain intact.
claims.qualification: The draft has no deployment or CI validation claim. It cannot revoke an old running provider, does not make storage read-only, and does not repair a defect in shared initialization.

claims.finding: Doctor checks each configured member with the existing binding validator, prints its store and concrete refusal reason, and continues after failures. This section does not initialize, provision or repair memory. A valid-binding result is not a full database-health or backend-capability assessment.
claims.qualification: Normal configuration loading still applies, and SQLite identity reads may create transient WAL coordination files while preserving the database and committed WAL content. Do not describe the entire CLI command as making no filesystem writes.

claims.finding: The documented compact-revisions command is an explicit offline owner operation that previews and optionally removes selected old accepted snapshots while preserving current content, every proposal and each record's latest accepted snapshot. It requires stopped writers, a verified complete archive, an exact preview count and a separate checked SQLite backup for apply. It does not run VACUUM or promise secure erasure.
claims.qualification: This is a source-contract review only; no compaction, SQL maintenance or product command was executed. It does not change the statement that V2 has no automatic accepted-history pruning.

one_commit_rollback_assessment.source_control_fact: The exact feature revision is one commit above the named parent. Reverting that change is a source-control operation encompassing both private V2 work and shared V1 repairs.
one_commit_rollback_assessment.operational_conclusion: A one-commit source rollback is not a supported data rollback for a populated V2 home. The owning spec explicitly prohibits running a pre-V2 binary over the home or repointing private members to V1. Preserve the stopped-state archive and use a reviewed maintenance withdrawal or repaired build while retaining identity and shared repairs.
one_commit_rollback_assessment.not_performed: No revert, checkout, branch change, reset, patch application, service stop, database operation or rollback validation was performed.

contradictions.lifecycle_runtime: No contradictory lifecycle or runtime behavior was identified in the inspected source paths. This is a bounded static review, not proof that every path or platform behaves correctly.
wording_to_avoid: V1 files are untouched or byte-identical after upgrade.
Existing V1 schedules automatically move to V2 or necessarily continue after the member binding changes.
Copy is one atomic all-or-nothing batch.
Every inferred correction applies automatically, or every verified owner correction requires a dashboard click.
Forget removes active chat text or has a direct Undo.
A restore confirmation proves that the backup is active.
Disabling private_provisioning_enabled stops existing providers or rolls the feature back.
One-commit feature reversion makes a populated home safe for the previous binary.
Doctor performs no filesystem writes or certifies private execution support.

The record-metadata module says older binaries can read/write original V1 tables, which is a table-compatibility statement. The maintenance contract separately forbids a pre-V2 binary over the populated home. These are different scopes, not evidence for operational rollback.
